description:
Purpose: generate instant, itemized quote estimates from the carriers
    Foresee supports, across the lines and states Foresee currently serves,
    in one call — the LIVE TODAY line at the end of this description names
    today's set. PRIMARY tool.

    `lines` is REQUIRED and is ONE map: each key names a line to price (e.g.
    "auto", "renters", "home" — plain words are fine), each value is that
    line's coverage ask as actual numbers. A line that isn't live yet comes
    back under `skipped` with honest copy saying where Foresee IS live,
    written to be relayed to the user as-is. For auto
    the ask has four axes — `bi` (bodily-injury liability, per-person/
    per-accident in $000s, e.g. "100/300"), `pd` (property-damage liability in
    $000s, e.g. 100), `coll_deductible` (collision deductible in dollars, e.g.
    500) and `comp_deductible` (comprehensive deductible in dollars, e.g.
    500); `um` and `medpay` are optional. A renters ask has four axes —
    `coverage_c` (personal-property/contents limit in dollars, e.g. 30000),
    `coverage_e` (personal liability in dollars, e.g. 100000), `coverage_f`
    (guest medical in dollars, e.g. 1000) and `deductible` (all-perils, in
    dollars, e.g. 500); `coverage_d` is optional. A home ask: `coverage_a`
    (the dwelling's replacement cost in dollars), `coverage_e` (e.g. 300000),
    `coverage_f` (e.g. 1000) and `aop_deductible` (all-other-perils
    deductible in dollars, e.g. 1000). There are no named coverage levels
    and the server never defaults: pass exact numbers. An omitted OPTIONAL
    axis (`um`, `medpay`, `coverage_d`) keeps each carrier's own
    default — the quote's per-coverage lines show what was rated. Any
    numbers work as the ask; the response carries the state's legal minimum,
    and each carrier's `price_ladder` prices every other rung, so a starting
    selection is easy to refine after the fact. An incomplete ask on a
    live line prices nothing and answers with `coverage_required` naming that
    line's own axes; an axis supplied with a value no carrier offers (`bi`
    "banana", a negative deductible) is refused the same way, naming the bad
    value and the format the axis takes. Each supported carrier is priced at
    exactly the selection given; a carrier with no such option appears in
    `failures` with the reason, as does one Foresee can't price for a line it
    was asked on (no program served there yet, or the carrier doesn't sell
    that line in the state) — a carrier never silently vanishes from a line's
    results. Priced results come back per line under `by_line`.

    Profile requirements: ZIP code, age (or dob) and — for auto — each
    vehicle's year/make/model are REQUIRED; they have no server-side
    fallback. A missing or mistyped one errors at the schema with guidance;
    a value that fits the schema but cannot rate ("not-a-zip", a negative
    age) comes back in `profile_required` naming it, with guidance on what
    the field takes. Use the profile schema's exact field names.

    Each carrier returns a **point estimate**
    (`monthly`) plus a `confidence_interval` that reflects only what's genuinely
    unresolvable (irreducible), NOT missing profile fields. A field the caller
    omits is filled with ONE declared value and reported in `assumptions` /
    `tighten_by` (the reducible "tell us X and we sharpen" gap) — the response
    is built to be presented early and refined, never widened into
    a vague range. An entry that carries `path` names the exact profile
    field to send the user's real answer under — never guess a key from the
    fact's name. A path-less entry (`incident_details`) is answered by
    completing the incident entries already sent (dates, fault, BI split), not
    under a fresh key. A `tighten_by` fact answers at its matching
    `assumptions` entry's path — or, for a flagged given value, its
    `input_flags` entry's path.

    Each carrier's `quote` carries every sub-coverage line (BI/PD/collision/
    comprehensive/UM…) with its rating steps, at the selection you passed (echoed
    as `coverage_selection`). Most carriers also carry a `price_ladder`: for each
    coverage lever of the line (auto: BI limit, PD limit, collision/comprehensive
    deductible; renters: deductible and the C/E/F limits; home: AOP deductible
    and the A/E/F limits) the exact
    price at every rung, one lever moved at a time with everything else
    held at the user's selection — the ladder is anchored at the selection you
    passed, so its `anchor.monthly` is the carrier's `monthly`. It answers
    limit/deductible what-ifs with real marginal prices.
    Every ladder number IS an exact re-rate; a combined change or an unlisted
    rung has no derivable price (rating is not linear), so those price only
    through a re-call with the new `coverage_selection`.
    

RESULT FORMAT: a compact machine text, not JSON. Its first line is Q <state> sel=<the coverage_selection priced, as JSON>; then a legend and a factor dictionary (f0=<name> …). Row types — C: carrier|entity|monthly|ci lo-hi. L: monthly $ per coverage line (already monthly, every carrier). F <fid>(<selected>)=v,v,…: one rating factor, one value per coverage in the L order; blank = not applied, one value = all coverages; suffix ? = estimated, ~ = derived, none = exact. D <lever> <selected>=option:±$: the change in the carrier's monthly for each option of that lever, everything else held at the selection — answer deductible/limit what-ifs from D without another call (new monthly = monthly + delta). Only state numbers that appear in the result or follow from monthly + a D delta; if a rung is not in D for a carrier, say the carrier has no such option rather than guessing.

When the user wants firm numbers straight from the carriers, offer live carrier quotes: Foresee agents complete the carriers' real quote flows via live_carrier_quotes (which explains the required disclosure + consent affirmation; no sign-in is needed). Instant quotes stay the first answer; live quotes are the follow-up.

LIVE TODAY: Foresee quotes auto in CA today.

CoverageSelectionInput.description:
The coverage to price, as actual numbers on named axes — the value type
of every entry in the ``lines`` map, so it publishes each line's axes side
by side (a line reads only its own; the map key says which apply).

Typed for the same reason as ``QuoteProfile``: with a bare dict the schema
published ``additionalProperties: true`` and nothing else, so callers
guessed key names ("bodily_injury") and burned a round trip on the
selection-required refusal before learning the real ones. The fields are
all optional HERE because completeness is judged server-side
(``coverage_ask``, per line): an incomplete selection must reach the
engines' rich ``coverage_selection_required`` payload — which names the
missing axes, a common choice, and (auto) the state's legal minimum — not
die as a generic schema validation error. ``extra="allow"`` keeps the
parser's accepted aliases (``bi_limit``, ``collision_deductible``,
``uim``…), the rarer home axes (B/C/D ratios, hurricane/water deductibles,
``endorsements``), and wider overrides working.

aop_deductible.description: HOME: all-other-perils deductible in dollars, e.g. 1000
aop_deductible.title: Aop Deductible

bi.description: Bodily-injury liability limit, per-person/per-accident in $000s, e.g. "100/300"
bi.title: Bi

coverage_a.description: HOME: dwelling limit in dollars — set it to the dwelling's replacement cost (the profile's property.replacement_cost when known)
coverage_a.title: Coverage A

coverage_c.description: RENTERS: personal-property (contents) limit in dollars, e.g. 30000 — the anchor an HO-4 rates off
coverage_c.title: Coverage C

coverage_d.description: RENTERS: loss-of-use limit in dollars — omit to keep the engine's carrier default (commonly a fixed ratio of the contents limit)
coverage_d.title: Coverage D

coverage_e.description: RENTERS/HOME: personal liability limit in dollars, e.g. 100000 (renters) / 300000 (home)
coverage_e.title: Coverage E

coverage_f.description: RENTERS/HOME: guest medical (medical payments to others) limit in dollars, e.g. 1000
coverage_f.title: Coverage F

deductible.description: RENTERS: all-perils deductible in dollars, e.g. 500
deductible.title: Deductible

medpay.description: Medical-payments limit in dollars, e.g. 5000 — omit to keep the carrier's default
medpay.title: Medpay

pd.description: Property-damage liability limit in $000s (NOT dollars), e.g. 100
pd.title: Pd

um.description: Uninsured/underinsured-motorist BI limit in $000s, e.g. "100/300" — omit to keep the carrier's default
um.title: Um

QuoteProfile.description:
The household being quoted: a line-neutral core plus per-line blocks
(#1106). Every fact has a declared posture (`foresee.postures`): a few
are REQUIRED — the ZIP, the applicant's age (or dob), and, when quoting
auto, each vehicle's year/make/model — because they have no neutral
rateable value; YOU supply those, inventing a concrete value from context
when the user was vague and telling them so. Everything else is optional:
omissions become explicit, priced assumptions (`assumptions` /
`tighten_by`), never a refusal.

The core carries facts about the people and where they live; the `auto`
block carries `drivers[]` and `vehicles[]`; the `property` block carries
the dwelling (home AND renters). A household that will only ever buy
renters simply has no `auto` block, and nothing about a car is assumed
for it.

Typed (rather than a bare dict) so the connector schema tells the model the
exact field names: an untyped profile made models guess keys ("zip"), the
value was silently ignored, and the engines rated a default location.
``extra="allow"`` keeps two things working unadvertised: the legacy flat
spellings (``vehicle_year``, ``spouse_dob``, ``currently_insured``,
3-year incident counts…), which fold onto the blocks — a flat key
disagreeing with a block is a hard error naming both — and richer keys
flowing through to the engines unchanged.

age.description: REQUIRED unless dob is passed. If the user was vague ('mid-20s'), pass a concrete age and present it as your assumption.
age.title: Age

auto.description: The auto line's facts: drivers[] and vehicles[]

companion_policies.description: Lines the household already HOLDS elsewhere, e.g. ["home"] — a held companion policy applies each carrier's multi-policy factor
companion_policies.title: Companion Policies

credit_range.description: 'Excellent' / 'Good' / 'Fair' / 'Poor'. Not a rating input in CA, HI, MA, or MI (credit-based auto rating is banned there) — omit it and don't ask shoppers in those states.
credit_range.title: Credit Range

dob.description: Date of birth, YYYY-MM-DD (alternative to age)
dob.title: Dob

education.description: Highest education level: 'No High School' / 'High School' / 'Vocational' / 'Some College' / 'Associate' / 'Bachelors' / 'Masters' / 'Doctorate'
education.title: Education

effective_date.description: Desired start date for the new policy, YYYY-MM-DD
effective_date.title: Effective Date

home_ownership_status.description: 'rent' / 'own with mortgage' / 'own outright' — bare 'own' is accepted; carrier forms ask which
home_ownership_status.title: Home Ownership Status

industry.description: Industry beside the occupation, e.g. 'Finance and Insurance' — GEICO's live quote form insists on it
industry.title: Industry

memberships.description: Organizations the applicant belongs to, e.g. ['Costco', 'AAA'] — group/affinity plans (CA §1861.12) discount on them
memberships.title: Memberships

months_at_residence.description: How long at the current address, in months
months_at_residence.title: Months At Residence

occupation.description: Occupation as carriers collect it, e.g. 'Accountant'
occupation.title: Occupation

prior_insurance.description: The insurance carried now — carrier, dates, limits held

property.description: The dwelling's facts — home and renters alike

state.description: Two-letter state code, e.g. 'CA' (derived from zip_code when omitted)
state.title: State

street_address.description: Street address (line 1) — sharpens territory rating and is required for live carrier submissions (logged as PII, never echoed)
street_address.title: Street Address

unit.description: Apartment/unit number (address line 2) — a renter or condo dweller in a multi-unit building needs it for live carrier submissions
unit.title: Unit

zip_code.description: REQUIRED — 5-digit garaging/home ZIP. ALWAYS pass the ZIP here, never under another key. If the user named only a city, pass that city's best-known ZIP and tell them the assumption.
zip_code.title: Zip Code

body_style.description: Trim / body style as the carrier lists it, e.g. "XLT AWD 4D GAS"
body_style.title: Body Style

bought_new.description: Whether the vehicle was new when bought (Allstate asks)
bought_new.title: Bought New

cost.description: What the vehicle cost new, whole dollars — some carriers' live quote forms (Kemper) insist on it
cost.title: Cost

garaging_zip.description: ZIP where THIS vehicle is garaged, when it differs from the household's zip_code — auto rating keys on the garaging territory, so a stated garaging ZIP is what gets rated

purchase_date.description: When the vehicle was bought — ISO 8601, "2021-06" or "2021" welcome
purchase_date.title: Purchase Date

One citation, as it will be declared. Dated, because carriers

kind.title: Kind

on.description: When it happened — ISO 8601, reduced precision welcome: "2024", "2024-06", or "2024-06-15". A year IS a date.
on.title: On

BundleSummary.description:
One carrier's bundle arithmetic when a call prices several lines
together. Totals are two REAL ratings of the same profile — the carrier's
multi-policy factors applied and cleared — never a percentage: the
factors apply per line and per coverage, and each shows in that line's
own quote cell like any other applied factor. This block only adds the
cross-line sums those cells cannot carry.

bundle_total.description: Monthly total across those lines rated together — the sum of this carrier's headline `monthly` in each line's by_line cell
bundle_total.title: Bundle Total

lines.description: The lines this carrier priced together
lines.title: Lines

standalone_total.description: Monthly total for the same lines each rated alone
standalone_total.title: Standalone Total

BundleSummary.title: BundleSummary

CarrierQuoteSummary.description: One carrier's headline in a quote result's structuredContent.

carrier_quote_url.description: The carrier's own quoting portal — where a purchase completes
carrier_quote_url.title: Carrier Quote Url

warnings.description: Per-carrier honesty notes — off-ladder-ask divergence, unconfirmed eligibility, no direct purchase path — relay them with the price
warnings.title: Warnings

CarrierQuoteSummary.title: CarrierQuoteSummary

LineQuoteSummary.description:
One priced line's headline block inside ``by_line``: the ask, the
prices, and the declared honesty blocks — what was assumed, what to ask
the user to sharpen it, who couldn't price the ask and why, and which
given inputs these rates don't price. Surface all of them.

assumptions.description: Omitted facts priced at a declared stand-in value — relay them with the prices; never present an assumed price as a measured one. An entry carrying `path` names the exact profile field to send the user's real answer under; a path-less entry is answered by completing the incident entries already sent
assumptions.title: Assumptions

coverage_selection.description: The ask this line was priced at, echoed verbatim
coverage_selection.title: Coverage Selection

failures.description: Carriers that could not price this exact ask, each with the reason (limit not offered, eligibility…) — they dropped out, they are not cheap or missing
failures.title: Failures

input_flags.description: Given inputs that look wrong (e.g. an odometer reading sent as annual mileage)
input_flags.title: Input Flags

not_rated.description: Inputs the caller GAVE that these rates do not price (a second vehicle, rideshare use…) — relay each note verbatim
not_rated.title: Not Rated

tighten_by.description: The missing facts that most move the price — offer to re-quote with the user's answers, each sent under its matching assumptions (or input_flags) entry's `path`
tighten_by.title: Tighten By

LineQuoteSummary.title: LineQuoteSummary

outputSchema.description:
structuredContent of the quote tools: headline numbers only, keyed by
line from the first scan (#1106) so a second line's launch never diffs
this schema.

The content channel carries the full sub-coverage/ladder detail; this stays
concise on purpose, and carries no internal identifiers (GHI #1101).

bundle.description: Per-carrier bundle totals, keyed like by_line's carrier_key, when one carrier priced several of the asked lines together. Absent means no bundle pricing was computed — never present multi-line prices as bundled unless this block says so
bundle.title: Bundle

by_line.description: Each priced line's carriers, cheapest first
by_line.title: By Line

coverage_required.description: Lines needing a coverage ask, each naming its own axes
coverage_required.title: Coverage Required

example_arguments.description: On a profile_required refusal: a correctly-wrapped call to imitate — re-call with the user's facts in this shape
example_arguments.title: Example Arguments

presentation.description: How to present priced results — rides with them
presentation.title: Presentation

profile_required.description: Required profile facts still missing (field → what to pass). Nothing is priced while any is open: supply each — if the user didn't state one, pass your best concrete value and present it to them as your assumption
profile_required.title: Profile Required

skipped.description: Lines not priced, with the honest reason — relay it
skipped.title: Skipped
